match.reason: The closest bank point, eng-context-text, covers the same broad idea that context shapes texts, but it is written for senior VCE Units 1 and 2 and centres on reader context and historical events, while this Year 8 point asks students to see time, place and society in a text's language, attitudes and assumptions, so it needs a new card at the right depth.

note:
A fresh check found these problems in this version. Fix each one, and keep everything that is right:
- Question a, other: The clue 'Think about what the story treats as ordinary' uses the same word, 'ordinary', as the right option, so a student can match the words without understanding the idea.
- Question b, other: The clue 'One text shows an attitude of its time, but not everyone's' nearly restates the right option and rules out the 'every person' option, which gives the answer away.

rejected.title: Texts reflect contexts
card: Context is the time, place and society in which a text is made. A text carries signs of that context, even when it is not about it.
Language
the words and phrases a writer uses can belong to one period or place. A word that was common long ago may sound odd or out of date now.
Attitudes
a text can show what many people in its society believed or valued. It does not prove that every person then agreed.
Taken for granted

a text may treat something as normal without explaining it, because its first readers already knew it. Details such as travel by horse and cart, or no mention of phones, can show when a text was made.
rejected.remember: A text shows its context in its words, its attitudes and what it treats as normal.

a.q: A story written about 100 years ago has characters who send news by telegram and never question it. What does this most clearly show?
opts: Telegrams were an ordinary part of life when it was written
The writer disliked all forms of modern technology
The story is mainly about the history of the telegram
The writer wanted to teach readers how telegrams work
a.why: The characters treat telegrams as normal, so the story reflects a time when they were part of everyday life. It is not about the history of telegrams or a dislike of technology, because the writer simply takes them for granted.
a.clue: Think about what the story treats as ordinary.

b.q: A newspaper article from long ago says girls should leave school early to help at home, and treats this as common sense. What does this show about its context?
opts: It reflects an attitude common in the society of its time
It proves that every person at that time agreed with it
It shows the writer was unusually unkind to girls
It tells us nothing, as articles do not reflect their time
b.why: The article treats the idea as common sense, so it shows an attitude held in its society then. One article cannot prove that every person agreed, because a text reflects a context rather than speaking for everyone in it.
b.clue: One text shows an attitude of its time, but not everyone's.

a.q: A story has characters who send news by telegram and never question it. What does this most clearly show?
opts: The story was made in a time when telegrams were in use
The writer disliked all forms of modern technology

b.q: A newspaper article from long ago says girls should leave school early to help at home, and treats this as common sense. What does this show about its context?
opts: It reflects an attitude common in the society of its time
It proves that every person at that time agreed with it
It shows the writer was unusually unkind
It tells us nothing, as articles do not reflect their time
b.why: The article treats the idea as common sense, so it shows an attitude held in its society then. One article cannot prove that every person agreed, because a text reflects a context rather than speaking for everyone in it.
b.clue: One text shows an attitude of its time, but not everyone's.

a.best: The story was made in a time when telegrams were in use

b.best: It reflects an attitude common in the society of its time

problems.detail: A story set in the past, such as historical fiction, can show telegrams as ordinary without being made in that time. The right option says the story was 'made' then, which a careful student could question. Saying 'set in or made in', or describing the story as an old one, would remove the doubt.

check.summary: Card and questions are accurate and match the point. One small wording issue: question a ignores historical fiction, where a modern story can treat telegrams as normal.
